title: Agent definition
description: The canonical, provider-agnostic definition of an agent (ADR-013), as the official definitions repository publishes it. Each adapter compiles it into its provider's native dialect rather than the platform maintaining one definition per provider — that compilation, and the drift it is compared against afterwards, is the adapter's job (T-052) and not part of this contract. What a project layers on top of this definition — the display name it uses, the content of the personalization section, the permissions it grants — lives in the project's own agents.json, never here.

role.description: The canonical role this agent plays. A flow names the participants of a stage by role, so an agent without one can take part in no flow. It is deliberately not the same field as the definition's id: two definitions can play the same role.

name.description: How the catalog names this definition — Architect, not Andrés. It is the name a card shows before anybody installs it, so it is not translated and it is not the persona name a project ends up using.

defaultDisplayName.description: The person-like name the platform ships this agent with. A project renames it through its personalization layer, and uniqueness of the name among the agents of a project is decided there, where all of them are visible at once.

description.description: What this agent is responsible for, in the languages the marketplace shows.

requiredCapabilities.description: What this agent needs from a provider to be installable. The definition is where this is declared and the marketplace manifest is where it is indexed: T-060 generates the manifest from the definitions, so the two can never be two opinions. An empty list says the agent asks nothing special of the provider.

instructions.description: The file holding the agent's canonical instructions, relative to this definition's own root. The body lives in markdown rather than in a string of this document: the personalization layer is diffed and merged against it when the platform updates (01-definicion-producto.md, section 4.5), and a diff over an escaped JSON string is a diff nobody can read. ADR-013 fixes the definition format as JSON so the platform maintains one format instead of one per provider — not that every byte has to sit inside the JSON.

personalization.description: The delimited section a project owns. The platform provides the definition; the team's names, conventions and adjustments go here and are never overwritten by an update (01-definicion-producto.md, section 4.5).

anchor.description: The token in the instructions that the adapter replaces with the project's personalization when it compiles. That the instructions actually contain it, exactly once, is checked by the core: this document cannot see the file it names.

providerSettings.description: Provider-specific settings this definition ships with, keyed by provider id — the second of the two configuration levels, the first being everything above it that is provider-agnostic. The shape of each value is owned by that provider's adapter, not by this schema; the key is not, because a typo in a provider id would silently address a provider that does not exist. The pattern is spelled out rather than referenced because a patternProperties key is a literal regular expression, and patternProperties is what a propertyNames constraint has to become for its rejection to name the field it came from; a test keeps this copy equal to the one in common.
